note: Re-judged 2026-11-15 after 22be149a08 changed the positive TestRFC5036DistinctLSRIDFormsAdjacency: sendHello lost its logger and now returns the write error, and the test fails at once on it (approved by a ze-test-judge); before, a failed write was only logged at Debug and surfaced later as the read timeout, so no assertion was removed and the failure is now attributed to its cause. RFC 5036 Section 3.1: "The first four octets identify the LSR and MUST be a globally unique value." Global uniqueness is an operator property; what ze owns is that every LDP Identifier it sends carries the configured lsr-id and that it refuses its own identifier from the wire. Positive: a distinct-LSR Hello forms the adjacency, and the headers of the Hello sendHello puts on a real UDP socket and of the Initialization runSession sends on a session built by sessionConfigForAdj both carry the engine's 192.0.2.77. Negative (unit unchanged): a Hello carrying ze's own LSR ID forms no adjacency and fires no callback; processDiscoveryPacket's own-LSR-ID return precedes the new discard counting and is unchanged.
